context: 6 Conclusion When the domain sizes of the components and base objects used by the implementation are all equal to b and n ≤ bk − bk + k, our obstruction-free, single-updater lower bound of 1 n−1 n−1 2 · (k + b − logb 2 ) asymptotically matches our obstruction-free, multi-updater upper bound of k + ⌈ b−1 ⌉. For all values of n, we conjecture that k + ⌈ nb ⌉ base objects with n domain size b are required by any obstruction-free, multi-updater, n-process implementation of a scannable object with k fully reusable components that have domain size b. When n > bk −bk+k, we gave an obstruction-free, single-updater lower bound of 12 ·(bk−1 − (b−1)k+1 b ) base objects. If b is a constant, then this asymptotically matches the wait-free, single-updater implementation from bk binary registers in Section 1. This means that, in order to prove a space lower bound better than bk for larger values of n, we need to consider more complex executions that contain concurrent Apply operations. We may also be able to improve our lower bound by considering stronger progress requirements like lock-freedom or wait-freedom.
